preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 40 for line in stdin.splitlines()[0:1]) and all(1 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= 1000 for line in stdin.splitlines()[0:1])
preconditions.description: The first line contains two integers n (1 ≤ n ≤ 40) and k (1 ≤ k ≤ 1000), representing the number of castles and liters of liquid, respectively.

preconditions.expression: len(stdin.splitlines()) == n + 1 and all(len(line.split()) == n for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: The input consists of exactly n + 1 lines: the first line with n and k, followed by n lines of adjacency matrix rows.

preconditions.expression: all(all(ai_j in {0, 1} for ai_j in line.split()) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each adjacency matrix entry ai_j is either 0 (no wall) or 1 (wall exists).

preconditions.expression: all(line.split()[i] == line.split()[j] for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for i in range(n) for j in range(n) if i != j and line.split()[i] == '1' and line.split()[j] == '1')
preconditions.description: The adjacency matrix is symmetric (ai_j = aj_i for all i, j).

preconditions.expression: all(line.split()[i] == '0' for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for i in range(n))
preconditions.description: No castle has a wall to itself (ai_i = 0 for all i).

postconditions.description: The output is a string representing the maximum possible sum of stabilities of the walls, where stability of a wall between castles a and b is x_a * x_b, and the sum of all x_i equals k. The output must be accurate within an absolute or relative error of 1e-6.

postconditions.expression: max_sum == sum(x[i] * x[j] * int(adj_matrix[i][j]) for i in range(n) for j in range(i + 1, n)) for some x in [tuple(xi) for xi in product([float(x) for x in [0.0, 1.0]], repeat=n) if sum(xi) <= k + 1e-9] if abs(sum(xi) - k) <= 1e-9
postconditions.description: The maximum sum is achieved by some distribution of liquid x_1, ..., x_n (each ≥ 0) summing to exactly k, where the sum of stabilities is maximized.
